Exceeded 10% of Prior Year Revenue ◦ Unprecedented client retention rate of approximately 97%; Strongest in Company history with multiple lines of business and countries surpassing that level ◦ Net New business at 6.8% of prior year revenue; Well above annual target of 4% to 5% • Revenue +9%; Organic Revenue +10% ◦ Revenue: FSS United States +6%, FSS International +15%; Organic Revenue: FSS United States +8%, FSS International +12% ◦ Growth driven by broad-based Net New business and base business volume • Operating Income +16%; Adjusted Operating Income (AOI) +13% 1 ◦ Benefited from accelerated revenue growth, supply chain efficiencies, and productivity gains driven by effective cost management ◦ Operating Income and AOI growth would have been approximately +19% and +15% 1 , respectively, if not for incremental incentive-based cash and equity compensation charges from the outperformance in key operating metrics • GAAP EPS +33% to $1.62; Repurchased approximately 3 million shares in fiscal 2026 and subsequent to year-end Q4 YEAR-OVER-YEAR SUMMARY • Revenue +5%; Organic Revenue +12% ◦ Growth led by substantial new business and higher client retention levels, including 1% contribution from Aramark Nexus; Adjusted EPS +25% 1 to $0.71 ◦ Continued execution of top and bottom-line financial performance; Incentive-based compensation charges referenced above impacted GAAP EPS and Adjusted EPS by $0.07, or 22% and 13% 1 , respectively FOLLOWING FISCAL 2026 YEAR-END • Board Authorized New $1 Billion Share Repurchase Program; Raised Quarterly Dividend by 17% ◦ Extensive flexibility to return capital to shareholders while continuing to strategically invest in the business; New program replaces existing $500 million share repurchase authorization ◦ Fourth consecutive year of double-digit dividend growth; Reflects the strength of the diverse, high-performing portfolio and a balanced approach to capital allocation 1 On a constant-currency basis Note: The prior year fourth quarter and full year results of Fiscal 2025 included a 53rd week of operations. Organic Revenue is based on 52 weeks for comparability purposes Philadelphia, PA, November 16, 2026 - Aramark (NYSE: ARMK) today reported results for the fourth quarter and full year of fiscal 2026. “Fiscal 2026 was a phenomenal year for Aramark, defined by unprecedented performance across the Company, with this momentum continuing into the new fiscal year,” said John Zillmer, Aramark CEO. “Our achievements included 1) record gross new business wins of $1.9 billion; 2) an all-time high client retention rate of approximately 97%; 3) the launch of Aramark Nexus in April as a complement to our existing portfolio, which is already contributing to revenue and profitability; 4) the addition of $1.3 billion in new purchasing spend to our Global Supply Chain network; and 5) a reduction in our leverage ratio to 2.7x, our lowest level in nearly two decades. I couldn’t be more proud of our teams, whose unwavering commitment to serving clients drove record results across key operating metrics as we concluded the fiscal year.” Zillmer continued, “Our hospitality culture and results-driven focus, grounded in growth and disciplined execution, have strengthened our financial position and provided significant flexibility to return capital to shareholders. This sustained performance supported the Board’s decision to authorize a new $1 billion share repurchase program and increase our quarterly dividend by 17%.” FISCAL 2026 SUMMARY Consolidated revenue was $20.1 billion, an increase of 9% year-over-year, as a result of broad-based Net New business and base business volume, which more than offset an estimated 2% impact from the 53rd week of operations in the prior year. The effect of currency translation increased revenue in the year by $183 million. Organic revenue, which excludes the impact of the 53rd week and currency translation, grew 10% compared to the prior year period. Organic revenue growth was greater than 8% in FSS United States and exceeded 12% in FSS International. Profitability growth benefited from increased revenue, supply chain efficiencies, and productivity gains. Operating Income and AOI in the year were impacted by incremental incentive-based cash and equity compensation charges of approximately $26 million associated with record achievements across key operating metrics, including Net New Business and Free Cash Flow. Operating Income and AOI would have increased year-over-year by an estimated 19% and 15% 1 , respectively, without these incentive-based compensation charges — with operating income and AOI margin expansion each at approximately 40 basis points 1 . FOURTH QUARTER RESULTS Consolidated revenue was $5.3 billion in the fourth quarter, a 5% increase year-over-year on a GAAP basis, with the 53rd week in the prior year period impacting reported growth by an estimated 7%. Organic revenue increased 12% compared to the prior year period. Revenue and Organic Revenue growth were primarily driven by substantial new business and higher client retention levels across the Company's lines of business and geographies. In addition, Aramark Nexus contributed 1% to revenue growth in the fourth quarter, as the business began to scale its premium hospitality services. • FSS International maintained its strong growth trajectory driven by new business as well as high client retention levels, with contributions across regions, notably in the U.K., Canada, and Chile. Top performing industries included Business & Industry, Education, and Extractive Services. Revenue on a GAAP basis reflected a $2 million reduction due to the effect of currency translation. CASH FLOW AND CAPITAL STRUCTURE Net cash provided by operating activities increased 7% to $989 million in fiscal 2026 and Free Cash Flow grew 26% to $573 million, a record for the Company. The unprecedented cash flow result was led by stronger profit generation, effective management of capital expenditures, and a continued focus on working capital. In the fourth quarter, the Company had a significant source of cash driven by Collegiate Hospitality, consistent with Aramark's historical seasonality. The Company's leverage ratio improved over 50 basis points to 2.7x at the end of fiscal 2026, as Aramark's operational performance and $225 million in Net Debt reduction translated into a strengthened balance sheet. In the fiscal year and subsequent to year-end, Aramark repurchased nearly 3 million shares of stock. At fiscal year-end, the Company had cash availability of over $2.3 billion. SHARE REPURCHASE PROGRAM AND DIVIDEND DECLARATION As a result of the Company's continued revenue growth, enhanced profitability, and cash flow generation capabilities, the Company has now surpassed its stated leverage goal. As a result, Aramark's Board of Directors authorized a new $1 billion share repurchase program, demonstrating strong confidence in the business and anticipated significant growth opportunities ahead. The new authorization will replace the previous $500 million program from November 2024, under which Aramark repurchased approximately 7 million shares. The share repurchase program does not have a fixed expiration date, providing Aramark with the flexibility to repurchase shares opportunistically. Page 4 Under the new share repurchase program, repurchases can be made from time to time using a variety of methods, including open market purchases, privately negotiated transactions, accelerated share repurchases, and Rule 10b5-1 trading plans. The size and timing of any repurchases will depend on a number of factors, including share price, general business and market conditions, and other factors. Aramark's Board of Directors also approved a 17% increase to Aramark's quarterly dividend. The dividend of $0.14 per share of common stock will be payable on December 16, 2026, to stockholders of record at the close of business on December 4, 2026. BUSINESS UPDATE In fiscal 2026, Aramark capitalized on extensive new business opportunities, resulting in annualized gross new business wins of $1.9 billion — greater than 10% of prior year revenue. The Company also achieved a client retention rate of approximately 97% with retention strength demonstrated across the portfolio. Combined, this represented unprecedented annualized Net New business for Aramark at 6.8% of prior year revenue, well above the Company's Net New business target. Aramark believes the new business pipeline across the organization is significant, including opportunities in multiple lines of business and geographies immediately ahead. Aramark Nexus continues to gain momentum as the Company works closely with its partners to deliver premium hospitality services to complex and often remote operating environments. Aramark is also focused on driving profitability through its multiple operating levers, which include leveraging technology to drive operating cost efficiencies, differentiated supply chain capabilities, and above-unit cost management, all building upon the Company's extensive scale. OUTLOOK The Company provides its expectations for organic revenue growth, Adjusted Operating Income growth (constant currency), Adjusted Earnings per Share growth (constant currency) and Net Debt to Covenant Adjusted EBITDA ("Leverage Ratio") on a non-GAAP basis, and does not provide a reconciliation of such forward-looking non-GAAP measures to GAAP due to the inherent difficulty in forecasting and quantifying certain amounts that are necessary for such reconciliations, including adjustments that could be made for the effect of currency translation. The fiscal 2027 outlook reflects management's current assumptions regarding numerous evolving factors that are difficult to accurately predict, including those discussed in the Risk Factors set forth in the Company's filings with the United States Securities and Exchange Commission. Page 6 Selected Operational and Financial Metrics Adjusted Revenue (Organic) Adjusted Revenue (Organic) represents revenue, adjusted to eliminate the impact of currency translation and the estimated impact of the 53rd week in fiscal 2025. Adjusted Operating Income Adjusted Operating Income represents operating income adjusted to eliminate the impact of amortization of acquisition-related intangible assets; severance and other charges and other items impacting comparability. Adjusted Operating Income (Constant Currency) Adjusted Operating Income (Constant Currency) represents Adjusted Operating Income adjusted to eliminate the impact of currency translation. Adjusted Net Income Adjusted Net Income represents net income attributable to Aramark stockholders adjusted to eliminate the impact of amortization of acquisition-related intangible assets; severance and other charges; loss on equity investments, net; the effect of debt repricing and repayments on interest expense, net, and other items impacting comparability, less the tax impact of these adjustments. The tax effect for Adjusted Net Income for our United States earnings is calculated using a blended United States federal and state tax rate. The tax effect for Adjusted Net Income in jurisdictions outside the United States is calculated at the local country tax rate. Adjusted Net Income (Constant Currency) Adjusted Net Income (Constant Currency) represents Adjusted Net Income adjusted to eliminate the impact of currency translation. Adjusted EPS Adjusted EPS represents Adjusted Net Income divided by diluted weighted average shares outstanding. Adjusted EPS (Constant Currency) Adjusted EPS (Constant Currency) represents Adjusted EPS adjusted to eliminate the impact of currency translation. Covenant Adjusted EBITDA Covenant Adjusted EBITDA represents net income attributable to Aramark stockholders adjusted for interest expense, net; provision for income taxes; depreciation and amortization and certain other items as defined in our credit agreements required in calculating covenant ratios and debt compliance. We also use Net Debt for our ratio to Covenant Adjusted EBITDA, which is calculated as total long-term borrowings less cash and cash equivalents. Free Cash Flow Free Cash Flow represents net cash provided by (used in) operating activities less net purchases of property and equipment and other. Management believes that the presentation of free cash flow provides useful information to investors because it represents a measure of cash flow available for distribution among all the security holders of the Company. Net New Business Net New Business is an internal statistical metric used to evaluate our new sales and retention performance. The calculation is defined as the annualized value of gross new business less the annualized value of lost business. In comparisons to prior year revenue, Gross New Business and Net New Business as a percentage of revenue is measured against FY25 52-week revenue for comparability purposes. We use Adjusted Revenue (Organic), Adjusted Operating Income (including on a constant currency basis), Adjusted Net Income (including on a constant currency basis), Adjusted EPS (including on a constant currency basis), Covenant Adjusted EBITDA and Free Cash Flow as supplemental measures of our operating profitability and to control our cash operating costs. We believe these financial measures are useful to investors because they enable better comparisons of our historical results and allow our investors to evaluate our performance based on the same metrics that we use to evaluate our performance and trends in our results. These financial metrics are not measurements of financial performance under generally accepted accounting principles, or GAAP. Our presentation of these metrics has limitations as an analytical tool and should not be considered in isolation or as a substitute for analysis of our results as reported under GAAP. You should not consider these measures as alternatives to revenue, operating income, net income, earnings per share or net cash provided by (used in) operating activities, determined in accordance with GAAP. Adjusted Revenue (Organic), Adjusted Operating Income, Adjusted Net Income, Adjusted EPS, Covenant Adjusted EBITDA and Free Cash Flow as presented by us may not be comparable to other similarly titled measures of other companies because not all companies use identical calculations. Page 7 Explanatory Notes to the Non-GAAP Schedules Amortization of Acquisition-Related Intangible Assets - adjustments to eliminate the impact of amortization expense recognized on acquisition-related intangible assets. Severance and Other Charges - adjustments to eliminate severance expenses in the applicable period ($11.1 million for fiscal 2026, $23.8 million for the fourth quarter of 2025 and $36.4 million for fiscal 2025). Gains, Losses and Settlements impacting comparability - adjustments to eliminate certain transactions that are not indicative of the Company's ongoing operational performance, including non-cash charges for the impairments of assets ($12.0 million for both the fourth quarter and fiscal 2026, $8.9 million for both the fourth quarter and fiscal 2025), non-cash charges related to information technology assets ($11.1 million for both the fourth quarter and fiscal 2026), charges to fully resolve legacy Vestis insurance claims ($8.5 million for both the fourth quarter and fiscal 2026), non-cash charges for the impairment of certain assets related to a business sold ($0.6 million for the fourth quarter of 2026 and $6.7 million for fiscal 2026), non-cash gain on lease remeasurement ($5.6 million for both the fourth quarter and fiscal 2026), multiemployer pension plan withdrawal charge, net of reversal ($4.8 million for fiscal 2026), legal and professional fees related to an antitrust review ($0.3 million for the fourth quarter of 2026, $2.7 million for fiscal 2026, $1.4 million for the fourth quarter of 2025 and $2.5 million for fiscal 2025), charges related to hyperinflation in Argentina ($0.7 million for the fourth quarter of 2026, $1.7 million for fiscal 2026, $2.7 million for the fourth quarter of 2025 and $5.7 million for fiscal 2025), other charges related to footprint reduction ($2.2 million for both the fourth quarter and fiscal 2026) and a charge for contingent consideration liabilities related to acquisition earn outs ($11.1 million for fiscal 2025). Loss on Equity Investments, net - adjustments to eliminate the impact of a non-cash charge for the impairment of an equity investment ($19.5 million for both the fourth quarter and fiscal 2025). Effect of Debt Repricing and Repayments on Interest Expense, net - adjustments to eliminate expenses associated with the refinancings and repayments by the Company in the applicable period such as non-cash charges for the write-off of unamortized debt issuance costs and discounts ($0.6 million for the fourth quarter of 2026, $1.0 million for fiscal 2026 and $2.5 million for fiscal 2025) and payment of third party costs ($0.7 million for fiscal 2026 and $5.8 million for fiscal 2025). Tax Impact of Adjustments to Adjusted Net Income - adjustments to eliminate the net tax impact of the adjustments to Adjusted Net Income calculated based on a blended United States federal and state tax rate for United States adjustments and the local country tax rate for adjustments in jurisdictions outside the United States. Adjustment to eliminate the impact of net valuation allowances recorded against deferred tax assets in foreign subsidiaries ($1.4 million charge for the fourth quarter of 2026, $9.5 million charge for fiscal 2026, $9.6 million benefit for the fourth quarter of 2025 and $21.2 million benefit for fiscal 2025) and eliminates the impact of the state tax treatment related to the sale of a minority interest ($4.4 million charge for fiscal 2025). Adjustment also eliminates a valuation allowance recorded based on the Company's ability to utilize foreign tax credits ($0.4 million charge for the fourth quarter of 2026, $3.8 million charge for fiscal 2026 and $2.9 million charge for both the fourth quarter and fiscal 2025), the benefit from release of certain reserves that were originally established due to CARES Act ($0.6 million benefit for fiscal 2026) and the tax related impact of the Company's spin-off of the Uniform segment, including disallowed transaction costs ($3.6 million charge for fiscal 2025). Effect of Currency Translation - adjustments to eliminate the impact that fluctuations in currency translation rates had on the comparative results by presenting the periods on a constant currency basis. Assumes constant foreign currency exchange rates based on the rates in effect for the prior year period being used in translation for the comparable current year period.
